papers.title_in_file: Classification on Emucore - Quantum Computing Inc
papers.what_it_is: A QCi web tutorial that runs a notebook classifying RAVDESS emotional speech with the EmuCore reservoir device and a linear readout, reporting train and test success rates.

assertions.value: The page states that QCi used its EmuCore reservoir technology to classify emotional speech files.
quotes: In this project, we have leveraged QCi's EmuCore reservoir technology to classify emotional speech files.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describing its own product's use.

assertions.value: The page defines reservoir computing as passing data through a randomly initialized neural network (the reservoir) and then training a simple linear model on the processed data.
quotes: Reservoir computing is an approach that involves passing data through a randomly initialized neural network (the reservoir) and then using the processed data to train a simple linear model downstream.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page's own definition of the term it uses, in the Reservoir Computing section.

assertions.value: The page states that reservoir-based models are easier to set up and less computationally expensive to train than traditional neural networks, and that the method requires less domain expertise.
quotes: Unlike traditional neural networks, reservoir-based models are easier to set up and less computationally expensive to train.
This method requires less domain expertise for different applications, making it highly versatile.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor's general statement about the method; no evidence on the page.
assertions.reader_inference: No comparison against a traditional neural network is run anywhere on the page.

assertions.value: The page states that EmuCore uses a time-delayed reservoir scheme, in which the reservoir layer holds only one physical node that acts as a large set of temporally spaced virtual nodes.
quotes: QCi's EmuCore technology employs a time-delayed scheme for reservoir computing.
the reservoir layer contain only one physical node that acts as a large set of temporally spaced virtual nodes.
assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describing its own product's architecture.

assertions.value: The page states that the setup uses a Recurrent Neural Network architecture as the reservoir, and that the conventional reservoir computer shown in its schematic is hard wired to accommodate RNN models.
quotes: In our setup, we use a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) architecture as our reservoir.
This architecture is hard wired to accommodate RNN models.
assertions.reader_inference: The page describes the reservoir as an RNN and also as a single physical node with virtual nodes; the code section connects to the EmuCore device rather than running an RNN, so the RNN passage reads as background.

assertions.value: The authors state that they used the RAVDESS Emotional Speech Dataset, which consists of 1440 audio files generated by 24 speakers and corresponding to 8 different emotions, with the aim of building a model that detects which emotion an audio file corresponds to.
quotes: In this study, we used the RAVDESS Emotional Speech Dataset.
RAVDESS dataset consists of 1440 audio files, generated by 24 speakers, which correspond to 8 different emotion.
The aim is build a model that can detect which emotion an audio file corresponds to.
assertions.certainty_reason: The page's statement of its own dataset in the Dataset section.

assertions.value: The code sets 24 actors and 19 training actors, shuffles the actor list randomly, and takes the first 19 as training actors; files from the other actors go to the test set.
assertions.anchor: Setting up the parameters; Loading the dataset
quotes: # Select the first NUM_TRAIN_ACTORS actors from the shuffled list for training
assertions.certainty_reason: The page's own code states the split.
assertions.reader_inference: The shuffle shows no random seed, so the particular split behind the reported scores is not reproducible from the page. Training and test sets hold different speakers.

assertions.value: The code takes the audio segment from index 50001 to 125000, resamples it to 12e3 Hz, and converts it to a cochleagram with the Lyon passive ear model using decimation factor 77 and ear_q 8.
assertions.anchor: Convert audio data to a cochleagram; Setting up the parameters

assertions.value: The printed output for most files shows a cochleagram shape of (243, 77), meaning 243 time steps by 77 features; a few files show (974, 77).
assertions.anchor: Loading the dataset and preparing to train the model (output)
assertions.reader_inference: Reading 243 as time steps and 77 as features follows from NUM_F = 77 in the code; the page does not label the axes.

assertions.value: The code configures the EmuCore reservoir with voltage bias 0.3, gain 0.65, 800 nodes, 800 taps, feature scaling 0.5, density 1 and 77 input features.
The code passes each file's cochleagram through the EmuCore client and asserts that the output has as many columns as there are nodes, replacing the 77 input features with 800 node responses.
quotes: # Ensure the number of features in the output data matches the number of nodes

assertions.value: The code trains a scikit-learn LinearRegression model with an intercept on the reservoir outputs, with one-hot labels rescaled to {-1, 1} and repeated for every time step of a file; the page states that the score is measured on the training data.
assertions.reader_inference: The page computes clf.score on the training data but does not print it.

assertions.value: The code predicts for each file by averaging the model's outputs over the file's time steps, then counts a file as correct when the highest-valued class is the file's true class; the success rate is the fraction of correct files.
assertions.anchor: Process Training Data; Calculate the accuracy of predictions
assertions.certainty_reason: The page's own metric code (named WSR_MSE there).
assertions.reader_inference: Despite its name and its docstring about weighted symbol rate mean squared error, the function computes plain top-1 accuracy.

assertions.value: The authors report a success rate of 0.654 on the training data and 0.517 on the test data for the emotion task.
assertions.anchor: Process Training Data / Process Test Data (output)
assertions.reader_inference: With 8 classes, chance accuracy is 0.125, so the test result is above chance. The page gives one run on one random actor split, no error bars, and no comparison to a model without the reservoir or to published RAVDESS results; the gap between training and test rates shows weak generalization to unseen speakers.
